t: Maximum Total Reward Using Operations II
o: After sorting, we choose a subset of values taken in increasing order where each taken value exceeds the running sum; equivalently a knapsack-style reachability question over sums up to 2·max(V) ≤ 1e5. We track which totals x are achievable; taking value v is legal only from states x < v. Bitset parallelism turns the O(n·V) DP into roughly O(n·V/64).
k: Sort ascending; a value v can only be added when the current sum x < v, so mask the DP to states below v before shifting.
Reachable sums never exceed 2·max(rewardValues), bounding the bitset at ~1e5 bits.
Answer = highest set bit of the final reachability mask.

a.i: dp is a bitmask where bit x means sum x is achievable. Process values in increasing order; for value v, newly reachable sums are (dp restricted to bits < v) shifted left by v. Restricting to bits < v enforces the x < v rule exactly, and increasing order guarantees each value is usable when considered.
s: Sort rewardValues ascending; allocate a bitset of size 2·max+1 with bit 0 set.
For each v: compute low = dp & ((1<<v)-1); dp |= low << v.
After all values, return the index of the highest set bit.
a.t: O(n·V/64) — each of n values triggers a masked shift over a V-bit mask processed in machine words

a.n: Approach 2: Boolean DP without bitset (conceptual baseline)
a.i: dp[x] = can we reach sum x. For each sorted v, for every currently reachable x < v, mark x+v. This is the direct O(n·V) translation and clarifies correctness of the bitset version.
s: Iterate values ascending; snapshot reachable x < v and set dp[x+v] = True.
Scan down from 2*maxV for the first True.
a.t: O(n·V) — up to 2.5e9 simple operations in the worst case; too slow in Python but instructive

w: Use the bitset version everywhere; the plain DP is only for explanation. Pitfalls: forgetting to sort (the x < v rule depends on processing order), and off-by-one in the bitset size (sums can reach nearly 2·max). Follow-ups: reconstruct which values were taken (store parent pointers), or handle values up to 1e9 with coordinate compression on distinct values (at most n distinct, cap the useful prefix).
